message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals, but they belong to different orders—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria** (the group that contains all modern carnivores, odd‑toed ungulates, hoofed mammals, bats, and whales). That ancestor lived roughly **90 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous period.
